quick: 250-500 mg PO every 8 h (IR); 500 mg BID (ER)
ER with food; IR with or without food
Use if clearly needed (generally considered acceptable)
Use with caution in severe impairment
Renal function on prolonged use; signs of colitis
summary: Cefaclor is an oral second-generation cephalosporin used for respiratory, ENT, urinary and skin infections caused by susceptible organisms. Immediate-release is dosed every 8 hours; extended-release 500 mg twice daily with food. Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy and a notable serum-sickness-like reaction in children are key cautions.
indications: Otitis media due to susceptible S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, staphylococci and S. pyogenes
Pharyngitis and tonsillitis due to S. pyogenes
Lower respiratory tract infections including pneumonia
Acute bronchitis and acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis (ER)
Skin and skin-structure infections due to susceptible S. aureus and S. pyogenes

dosage.n: Severe infections / less susceptible organisms: 500 mg q8h
Take with meals; do not crush; 7-10 days

dosage.d: 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 8 h (max 1 g/day)
Use with caution; consider reduced dose

admin: Extended-release tablets must be taken with food and swallowed whole (not cut, crushed or chewed)
Immediate-release may be taken with or without food
Confirm penicillin/cephalosporin allergy history before use
Reserve for proven or strongly suspected susceptible bacterial infection
moa: Cefaclor is a bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits the final transpeptidation step of bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan synthesis, leading to cell lysis. It is stable against some beta-lactamases.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cefaclor or other cephalosporins
relative: History of gastrointestinal disease, particularly colitis

preg: Generally considered acceptable when clearly needed; cephalosporins have a long record of use in pregnancy without evidence of harm. Use if benefit justifies use.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding; only small amounts are excreted in milk. Monitor infant for diarrhea or thrush.
renal: Use with caution in severe renal impairment; consider dose reduction or extended interval and monitor, as cefaclor is renally eliminated.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment required for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Probenecid - reduces renal excretion, increases cefaclor levels
Warfarin - cephalosporins may potentiate anticoagulant effect (monitor INR)
minor: Antacids (ER form) - taken within 1 hour reduce ER absorption; separate dosing
interactions.food: Extended-release absorption is enhanced with food; immediate-release unaffected.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction (Benedict/Clinitest) tests and false-positive direct Coombs test.

monitoring: Signs of superinfection or C. difficile diarrhea
Signs of hypersensitivity or serum-sickness-like reaction
counsel: Take extended-release tablets with food and swallow whole
Finish the entire course even if you feel better
Report rash, joint pain, fever or persistent/bloody diarrhea
Tell your provider about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
Diarrhea may occur; report severe or persistent diarrhea
pk: Dosed every 8 h (IR) or every 12 h (ER)
Store at 20-25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Serum-sickness-like reaction (rash, arthralgia, fever) is characteristically associated with cefaclor, mainly in children
ER 500 mg BID is equivalent to IR 250 mg TID, not to 500 mg TID
Take ER with food to improve absorption
Largely renally cleared - caution in severe renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress and diarrhea. Treat symptomatically and supportively; consider gastric decontamination if a large recent ingestion. Hemodialysis can remove some cefaclor.
